title: The Interior of the Earth: Layers and Sources of Evidence

questions.question: The Kola Superdeep Borehole, the deepest ever drilled, reached a depth of about:
questions.rationale: The Kola Borehole reached roughly 12 km — the deepest direct penetration of the crust; the deepest mine (Mponeng) is only about 4 km.

questions.question: Which is the most important source of information about the Earth's interior?
questions.rationale: Seismic waves change speed and path when they cross material boundaries, revealing layer depths, states, and densities without any drilling.

questions.question: Continental crust (sial) is typically how thick?
questions.rationale: Continental crust spans roughly 30–70 km, while the denser oceanic crust (sima) is only about 5–10 km thick.

questions.question: The Mohorovicic (Moho) discontinuity, identified in 1909, separates:
options: The mantle and the outer core
questions.rationale: The Moho marks the base of the crust, where seismic waves speed up entering the denser mantle.

questions.question: The Gutenberg discontinuity lies at a depth of about:
questions.rationale: The Gutenberg discontinuity (~2,900 km) marks the mantle–outer core boundary; 700 km is Repetti and 5,100 km is Lehmann.

questions.question: What evidence shows that the outer core is liquid?
options: P-waves are completely blocked by the core
S-waves cannot pass through the outer core
Surface waves travel through it fastest
questions.rationale: S-waves travel only through solids, so their failure to cross the outer core proves it is liquid iron and nickel.

questions.question: Who discovered the solid inner core in 1936?
questions.rationale: Inge Lehmann identified the solid inner core at about 5,100 km depth from patterns in seismic wave arrivals.

questions.question: The mantle is approximately how thick?
questions.rationale: The mantle extends about 2,900 km from the base of the crust down to the Gutenberg discontinuity.

questions.question: The asthenosphere is best described as:
options: The rigid layer broken into tectonic plates
The weak, partly molten zone that is the main source of magma
The solid innermost sphere of the Earth
questions.rationale: The asthenosphere lies beneath the lithosphere, extends to roughly 400 km, behaves weakly, supplies magma, and carries the sliding plates.

questions.question: As depth increases toward the Earth's centre, temperature, pressure, and density:
questions.rationale: Temperature climbs to 5,000–6,000°C, pressure to over 3.5 million atmospheres, and density from about 2.7 to about 13.6 g/cm³ at the centre.
